name: Copallen
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Extinct unclassifiable language of Peru known only from a short colonial wordlist; no stress documentation possible.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page copa1238 (Hammarström, Forkel, Haspelmath & Bank). Unclassifiable; extinct; PE. JSON 'meds': Torero 1993 [46272], Anónimo 1897 [29841].
sources.note: Nothing; no references displayed on page, only the two wordlist-or-less entries in the JSON.

sources.citation: Loukotka, Čestmír. 1968. Classification of South American Indian Languages. Los Angeles: Latin American Center, UCLA. Entry 105 "Copallén, isolated language", p. 239, plus comparative table (Tabancale/Copallén/Chimú).
sources.note: Nothing. 'Copallén - extinct language once spoken in the villages of Llanque, Las Lomas, and Copallén, department of Cajamarca, Peru. [Jijón y Caamaño 1919, p. 393; Rivet 1934, p. 245, both only four words.]' Table gives kiet 'water', ismare 'house', chumak 'maize' with no stress marks.

sources.citation: Wikipedia, "Copallén language" (en) and "Idioma copallén" (es), citing Loukotka 1968 p. 239, Adelaar & Muysken 2004, Jiménez de la Espada 1965 [1881-97].
sources.note: Nothing; only the four words, location, and a speculative link of quiet 'water' to the toponymic element -cat (Cholón?).

sources.citation: Anónimo [1586]. "Relación de la tierra de Jaén". In Marcos Jiménez de la Espada (ed.), Relaciones Geográficas de Indias: Perú, tomo IV, pp. 28-33 (Copallén words on p. 30; ethnographic note in Apéndice p. LI). Madrid: Los Hijos de M. G. Hernández, 1897. (Glottolog ref 29841)
sources.note: Nothing. The sole primary attestation: four words in 16th-century Spanish orthography (quiet 'agua', chumac 'maiz', olaman 'leña', ismare 'casa'), no accent marks, no comment on pronunciation; Llanque and Copallén said to share 'una gente y lengua', Las Lomas del Viento 'hablan la lengua de Copallen'.

sources.citation: Adelaar, Willem F. H. & Pieter C. Muysken. 2004. The Languages of the Andes. Cambridge: Cambridge University Press (section on the languages of the Jaén area, ca. p. 401).
